## Method

* **Before-images (no git).** This checker fetched main's head `a000282a` (2026-10-14T03:22Z) through the GitHub

  Every `node_modules` link is relative and stays inside the mirror. Its `node_modules` was deleted at the end.

  wrong answer. Q3b and Q4b replace Q3 and Q4. P1, the own-child read capped at L2 without `max`, was red on the
  pre-round tests for the same reason, and P1b replaces it. That leaves 12 valid mutants out of 17.
* **Baselines.** pre "Tests 67 passed | 2 skipped (69)"; post "Tests 69 passed (69)".

## (1) The round's failing lines

### N-5: off-line finer vertices covered only one level deep. PINNED. CONFIRMED.

* **Source note.** Re-read whole: `checks/M0-a-03-notes.md:15`, together with the inventory row `hardening-inventory.md:291`.
* **Fixture.** `test/index/support.ts` `CHAIN` has exactly the note's coordinates:
  * the run A (0, 1000) → B (2000, 1006);
  * S1 (1100, 1003) at L2, S2 (500, 1002) at L3 and S3 (800, 1002) at L4.

  The checker recomputed each vertex's distance to every coarser route through it. All are within the 0.71 cm hot
  pixel: S1 is 0.3 below A–B; S2 is 0.5 above A–B and 0.64 above A–S1; S3 is 0.4 below A–B, 0.18 below A–S1 and 0.5
  below S2–S1.
* **Lines up.** All three lines run up to the top side. The note left the side open; the round chose up, and the
  checker agrees with the choice. With the lines up, the lower L1 face is its own child at L2 – L4, so the own-child
  path meets both slivers.
* **Tests added.** `query.test.ts` "along a run with finer vertices off their coarser routes three levels deep (CHAIN)"
  and `pointlocate.test.ts` "reads every coarser record on the level-n route three levels deep (CHAIN)". Both judge
  against their oracles in four states: static, grid, rebuilt and mixed.
* **The pins.** Each mutant below is alive on the pre-round tests and red on the round's tests. Each one fails exactly
  the CHAIN `pointLocate` test:
  * P3: the own-child record read one level finer than its own, `faceRouteRings(p, lm, slot, Math.min(level, lm + 1))`.
    This is the author's C2, re-killed independently. Pre "67 passed | 2 skipped"; post "1 failed | 68 passed".
  * P1b: the own-child record read at most at L2, `Math.max(lm, Math.min(level, 2))`. This depth was unreachable by
    OFFLINE. Pre "67 passed | 2 skipped"; post "1 failed | 68 passed".
* **Controls, red on both variants.**
  * P2 (own level) and P5 (`max(lm, level − 1)`) are red on OFFLINE `pointLocate`; on the post variant CHAIN is red as
    well.
  * Q3b and Q4b (query route pieces capped at L3 and at L2) are red on the fuzz, the oracle tests and both CHAIN tests:
    pre "8 failed" and "12 failed"; post "10 failed" and "14 failed".
* **One survivor: P4, the own-child read capped at L3 in `pointLocate`.** It is alive on both variants (67 + 2 skipped
  / 69).
  * On CHAIN it is equivalent. The L3 / L4 triangle S2–S3–S1 has area 150 and 302 boundary points, so by Pick's theorem
    it has no interior lattice point, and `pointLocate` takes only lattice points.
  * In general it is not equivalent. This checker's lawful probe `CHAIN4` kills it with
    `L4 at 1251,1004: expected [ 3, +0 ] to deeply equal [ 1, +0 ]`. CHAIN4 has an L4 vertex 0.5 cm off a
    non-horizontal L3 route, with 249 sliver lattice points. The probe is green on the tree's sources.
  * The round built the note's fixture as the note gives it, and the gap comes from the note's own coordinates. Under
    the blocker rule this is a further hardening test, not a failing line: note **N-s1c-1** (M4), with CHAIN4 given
    whole.

  * K4: the two keys swapped.
